dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1792 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json), and the families of 1791 were split again over the 1792 pages (items_from_1791.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by its own opening over all 1,629 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units (176 of 428 met the bar); every page was swept for seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers (sweep_new and sweep_recheck: the passages no item covers); every unit and passage that meets the bar was read, and the chosen items' openings were searched over all pages (phrase_hits.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN) as amended by the owner's choice B1 on 23 November 2026: an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; digests are not. As in R-01, items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35, a target, not a quota); one affair's items as in X-1800-01. The eligible items not chosen are listed with their counts and are not checked against the scans. Sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) apply as in every year.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1792 has 8 catalogue series, which are 8 papers: the National Gazette and the Gazette of the United States (Philadelphia), the New-Hampshire Gazette, and the General Advertiser (Portsmouth), the New Hampshire Gazetteer (Exeter), the Kentucky Gazette (Lexington), the Potowmac Guardian, and Berkeley Advertiser (its own news is dated at Martinsburg; the catalogue places it at Shepherdstown), the Mirrour (Concord, from 6 September) and the Phenix (Dover, one issue, 26 December). The release's map lists six misfiled RevX pages for 1792 (X-1792-04).

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Every finder item of 1792 in 3 or more papers (and of 1791 over the 1792 pages) was counted by its own opening over all 1,629 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units: 176 of 428 units met the bar. Reading them, with the sweep's passages, gave 236 items, and 2 more were read beside the chosen ones (238): 188 eligible and 50 below the bar. Four are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 25 are chosen (29 stories, 29 groups, 146 printings); 142 eligible items are listed as not chosen and 17 for the owner.
counted_item_by_item.The bar: Y-THIN: more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks (a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and at least 4. 1792 has 8 papers: the National Gazette, the Gazette of the United States, the New-Hampshire Gazette, the New Hampshire Gazetteer, the Kentucky Gazette and the Potowmac Guardian survive for the whole year (the Kentucky Gazette has no issue in October), the Mirrour from 6 September (none in October), and the Phenix in one issue, 26 December. The bar is 4, and 5 when the Phenix's issue falls in an item's weeks.
counted_item_by_item.Counted by their own words and opening: C-06 and C-07, from reading every printing of the chosen items and of the items they were weighed against: the French King's speech of 20 April is printed from its opening by 3 papers (the Potowmac Guardian prints only its conclusion, X-1802-06) and the Brussels accounts of 4 and 10 May by 3 each (other papers give the same news in their own words or in other paragraphs): below the bar. The Paris paragraph on Paul Jones (the National Gazette's is its own summary) and the letter from Ostend on M. La Fayette (the National Gazette prints only the paragraph that follows it) are printed by 4 of the 5 papers in print, not all; Mr. Seagrove's letter by 4 papers (a Philadelphia paragraph that sums it up, in 3, is not counted).
counted_item_by_item.Printed forms together: C-02: the Charleston paragraph on Mr. Bowles ('By a letter received in town from the Rock Landing', and 'A Charleston paper mentions, that'); the Baltimore report from Cape-Francois (the Potowmac Guardian's 'The last accounts from Cape Francois state', under Boston); the report of the Five Nations' deputation (as the Albany Gazette's, as a gentleman's from the Genesee country, and as an addition to another paragraph); the Paris paragraph on Paul Jones (two papers print it among deaths); the Dublin letter (two papers print it under Dublin without 'Extract of a letter'); the Petersburg paragraph (the Kentucky Gazette dates it Richmond, 5 May); the decree against M. La Fayette (the National Gazette gives the account before it in its own words).
counted_item_by_item.Letters printed together: X-1810-01: the President's letter of 16 January and the Secretary of War's statement; the President's message of 5 March and the King of France's letter.
counted_item_by_item.Printed again: C-08: the Potowmac Guardian prints the President's proclamation of September twice and the Kentucky Gazette five times; each printing counts (the 146 printings include them).
counted_item_by_item.Acts of Congress: The acts on the post-office, the protection of the frontiers, the mint and the militia are counted by their printings whole from the title; the lists of the session's acts that name them, and the House proceedings on their bills, are not counted (C-07).
counted_item_by_item.The Kentucky Gazette as edition 2: The archive files the Kentucky Gazette's 1792 issues as edition 2 (the issue of 7 January also as edition 1); the ledger uses the release's keys.
